rows.description: A component of IT architecture (together with applications and technology)
An enterprise scheme for classifying data by factors such as criticality, sensitivity and ownership
Procedures and tools to enable data to be classified, created in line with organisation policies
Identification of technology opportunities for the business
Organisational standards for infrastructure products and practices together with guidance on the selection of technology
An assessment of current and future technology trends and the potential opportunities and risks to the organisation
A plan for the technology, human resources and facilities that enables the current and future processing and use of applications

The required set of hardware, software and facilities that integrates an organisation’s IT assets

Scope note:  Specifically, this includes the equipment (including servers, routers, switches and cabling), software, services and products used in storing, processing, transmitting and displaying all forms of information for the organisation’s users.

A process framework that includes IT process structure and relationships (e.g., to manage process gaps and overlaps), ownership, maturity, performance measurement, improvement, compliance, quality targets, and plans to achieve them. It should provide integration amongst the processes that are specific to IT, enterprise portfolio management, business processes and business change processes. The IT process framework should be integrated into a quality management system (QMS) and the internal control framework.
An application system owner is the individual who has been assigned ultimate responsibility for a system.
A specification of internal and external IT organisational structure and responsibilities
Roles and responsibilities for IT personnel and end users that delineate between IT personnel and end-user authority, responsibilities and accountability for meeting the organisation’s needs
A report weighing the total expected costs against the total expected benefits of one or more actions to choose the best or most profitable option

A budget reflecting the priorities established by the enterprise’s portfolio of IT-enabled investment programmes, and including the ongoing costs of operating and maintaining the current infrastructure
A grouping of IT services managed and monitored to optimise business value
A grouping of IT projects managed and monitored to optimise business value
A set of fundamental controls that facilitates the discharge of business process owner responsibilities to prevent financial or information loss in an organisation
High-level statements of management intent and direction
Policies and procedures for IT HR, including recruitment and selection, conditions of employment, performance learning and development, behaviour and code of conduct, administration and support
Details of skills required by the IT organisation to meet business objectives
Outline of responsibilities of a position. It may often include to whom the position reports and specifications such as the qualifications or skills needed by the person in the job.

rows.wp: Users’ skills and competencies, including individual training
rows.description: Identification of IT knowledge or skill required to produce outputs in an organisation using IT. It should identify the individual competencies that need to be attained by a specific staff and the training required to achieve those competencies.
Roles and responsibilities for IT personnel and end users that delineate between IT personnel and end-user authority, responsibilities and accountability for meeting the organisation’s needs

Standards that define the process and activities required to acquire application software or an upgrade, including evaluation of the supplier’s financial stability, track record, resources and references from existing customers
Standards that define the process and activities necessary to produce quality software. It should include detailed procedures and practices for key IT development practices.
A system that outlines the policies and procedures necessary to improve and control the various processes that will ultimately lead to improved organisation performance
The quality improvement actions that are planned, who will be responsible and when they will be implemented

A process used to identify and evaluate risks and their potential effects

Scope note:  Risk assessment includes assessing the critical functions necessary for an organisation to continue business operations, defining the controls in place to reduce organisation exposure and evaluating the cost for such controls. Risk analysis often involves an evaluation of the probabilities of a particular event.
A report to senior management of high-risk actions, responsibilities and proposed actions
The co-ordinated activities to direct and control an organisation with regard to risk [ISO/IEC Guide 73:2002]
The actions planned to address identified risks, who will be responsible and when they will be implemented
Reports on the status of projects against planned milestones and resource usage, highlighting any issues potentially impacting the achievement of planned outcomes
Describes how risk management will be structured and performed on the project. It becomes a subset of the project management plan.
Guidance on the approach to be adopted for defining the scope and boundaries of managing projects, as well as the method to be adopted and applied to each project undertaken

A formal, approved document used to guide both project execution and project control. The primary uses of the project plan are to document planning assumptions and decisions, facilitate communication among stakeholders, and document approved scope, cost and schedule baselines. A project plan may be summarised or detailed.
A grouping of IT projects managed and monitored to optimise business value (see PO1)
A phase of a system development life cycle (SDLC) methodology that researches the feasibility and adequacy of resources for the development or acquisition of a system solution to a user need

Controls that achieve the business objectives of timely, accurate and reliable information. They consist of the manual and automated activities that ensure that information conforms to certain criteria—what COBIT refers to as business requirements for information. Those criteria are effectiveness, efficiency, confidentiality, integrity, availability, compliance and reliability.

Also known as an application or application system, it is computer software designed to help the user to perform singular or multiple related specific tasks. An application differs from an operating system (which runs a computer), a utility (which performs maintenance or general-purpose chores) and a programming language (with which computer programs are created).
Documented specification (at a high level) of the software and services to be acquired. It is used as a basis for procurement action.
An agreement, preferably documented, between a service provider and the customer(s)/user(s) that defines minimum performance targets for a service and how they will be measured

Availability and service continuity requirements should be identified on the basis of business plans, SLAs and risk assessments. Requirements should include access rights and response times as well as end-to-end availability of system components. Requirements should include, but not be limited to, access rights, service response times and end-to-end availability of services.
Acquired (or developed) system configured to meet business-defined requirements
System configured to meet the business-defined requirements after testing and installation in the production environment

The physical environment required for IT assets. It includes:
• The physical sites for IT equipment
• Physical security measures—Definition and implementation of procedures to grant, limit and revoke access to premises, buildings and areas
• Protection against environmental factors
• Physical facilities management, including power and communications equipment
Changes to organisational standards for infrastructure products and practices based on decisions made during acquiring and maintaining technology infrastructure
The specification of the information required to be provided to enable effective monitoring of the application, system or infrastructure
Knowledge about available IT infrastructure, where IT infrastructure is the set of hardware, software and facilities that integrates an organisation’s IT assets (see PO3)
An internal agreement covering the delivery of services that support the IT organisation in its delivery of services

rows.wp: User, operational, support, technical and administration manuals
rows.description: Technical communication documents intended to give assistance to people using, supporting or administering a particular system

rows.wp: Knowledge transfer requirements for a solution’s implementation
rows.description: The specification of the knowledge that needs to be transferred to business management, end users, and operations and support staff to enable effective management, use, operation and support of the part(s) of the application system or IT infrastructure

Material used to train business management, end users, and operations and support staff to enable effective management, use, operation and support of the part(s) of the application system or IT infrastructure

The specification of the requirements for managing customer-supplier relationships. It includes clearly defined roles, responsibilities and expectations in third-party agreements as well as monitoring processes.
Hardware or software procured as part of the acquisition process
A formal agreement regarding expectations and responsibilities between the parties
A documented procedure to record, classify, assess and approve RFCs
A documented procedure to apply changes to the production environment
A log of all change requests and the status in terms of assessment, approval (or rejection) and implementation
A record of the approval (or authorisation) for a change

Components of an infrastructure—or an item, such as a request for change, associated with an infrastructure—that is (or is to be) under the control of configuration management

Scope note:  CIs may vary widely in complexity, size and type, from an entire system (including all hardware, software and documentation) to a single module or a minor hardware component.
The documentation of known and accepted errors identified in testing (for identification in documented procedures together with any additional procedures required)
Handover of a system from development to testing to operations in line with an implementation plan

Documented plan on how to roll out the release. It should include identifying requirements for ensuring sign-off, packaging, regression testing, distribution, handover, status tracking, backup procedures and user notification.
An assessment and review of the completed working solution performed after a period of live running
Identified key controls that should be subject to monitoring, including frequency, possible procedures and thresholds for monitoring
A report reviewing contracted IT services
Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose
New or updated specifications of services required and defined by business needs, to be addressed by IT
An agreement, preferably documented, between a service provider and the customer(s)/user(s) that defines minimum performance targets for a service and how they will be measured

An internal agreement covering the delivery of services that support the IT organisation in its delivery of services
(see AI3)
The updated set of services that are managed by a service provider; is used to manage the entire life cycle of all IT services

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
A catalogue of third-party suppliers of IT products and services
Risks associated with the engagement or provisioning of third-party IT products and services
Information on IT resources available or needed to process IT workloads
A plan for the review of performance and capacity of IT resources to ensure that cost-justifiable capacity and performance are available to process the agreed-upon workloads as determined by the SLAs
Changes required to be made to infrastructure and applications

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Test results for contingency arrangements that ensure that IT systems can effectively recover from systems failure or disruption in the case of an adverse event
The criticality of particular IT infrastructure components that are under the control of configuration management

A plan for copying and storing data and other IT resources to protect against loss of integrity or availability of the original that includes procedures for backup and restoration of systems, applications, data and documentation according to business need, continuity plan and security requirements
The trigger points marking a major disruption on key functions and processes

rows.wp: Disaster service requirements, including roles and responsibilities
rows.description: Definition of requirements designed to return the organisation to an acceptable condition, including restoration of critical business functions, from an interruption in services

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Specification of the characteristics of security incidents that are used by the incident and problem management process

rows.wp: Specific training requirements on security awareness
rows.description: Requirements definition for the awareness training of individuals who potentially have access to the organisation’s information

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Change requirements in the context of IT security
Potential for threat sources to successfully exploit lapses in security either accidentally or intentionally
A high-level document defining an organisation’s information security philosophy, commitment preparedness and response in the context of business, risk and compliance requirements
Financial information pertaining to IT-related activities and operations

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Requirements for documentation updates pertaining to IT operations and use

A user request for advice or information; for a standard change; for access to an IT service, e.g., to reset a password; to provide standard IT services for a new user. Service requests are usually handled by a service desk, and do not require a formal RFC to be submitted.
Reports of unexpected events, an interruption or unplanned quality reduction to an IT service, which may involve an attack or series of attacks (compromise and/or breach of security)

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Reports on satisfaction levels of IT users on one or more of the following: IT services, application performance, incident/problem resolution, education and training
Details regarding a component of an infrastructure—or an item, such as a request for change, associated with an infrastructure—that is (or is to be) under the control of configuration management

rows.wp: RFC (where and how to apply the fix)
rows.description: A formal proposal for a change to be made, which includes details of the proposed change

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)

rows.wp: RFC (where and how to apply the fix)
rows.description:
A formal proposal for a change to be made, which includes details of the proposed change
(Repeated from DS9-WP2)

Records of the unknown underlying cause of one or more incidents. The cause is not usually known at the time a problem record is created, and the problem management process is responsible for further investigation.

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)

rows.wp: Known problems, known errors and workarounds
rows.description: Known error:  A problem that has a documented root cause and a workaround. Known errors are created and managed throughout their life cycle by problem management.

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)

rows.wp: Operator instructions for data management outcomes
rows.description: Procedural instructions for data storage/retention/archival arrangements, disposal, backup/restoration, and compliance with security requirements

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
An acknowledgement generated upon the initial lodgment of an incident

A serial or chronological record of design flaws or malfunctions that cause failures of one or more configuration items or IT services. Errors include mistakes made by persons or a faulty process that affects a configuration item or IT service.

Reports for the extent to which the execution of processes achieve their purpose

(Repeated from DS1-WP2)
Performance in terms of IT’s contribution to business objectives, functionality, stability, complexity, costs, strengths and weaknesses
Plan (including timeframe) showing remedial action in place to address non-compliance issues
A monitoring report that is part of the enterprise risk management (ERM) system that continuously identifies risk trends and events
Reporting on the performance of selected processes against agreed performance indicators

rows.wp: Report on effectiveness of IT controls
rows.description: Report outlining effectiveness of IT controls based on management assessment and independent assurance reviews

rows.wp: Catalogue of legal and regulatory requirements related to IT service delivery
rows.description: Reporting outlining legal and regulatory requirements and their impact on IT service delivery

rows.wp: Report on compliance of IT activities with external legal and regulatory requirements
rows.description: Report outlining compliance of IT activities with external legal and regulatory requirements based on management assessment and independent assurance reviews
Action taken to change an enterprise’s framework (its strategies, goals, policies responsibilities and activities) so that they meet the enterprise’s business goals
An assessment of the effectiveness of IT governance based on independent assurance

rows.wp: Expected business outcomes of IT-enabled business investments
rows.description: Documentation of an observable result or change in business performance, possibly supported by transaction-based metrics, resulting from new initiatives based on new or changed IT
A monitoring report of the enterprise governance of IT that identifies strategic issues such as technology capabilities, which creates a shared understanding between business and IT
A statement of approved risk appetite for IT based on and consistent with the enterprise risk appetite statement
